chapter: Left out of the jazz books; Tatum, Handy and family
title: Music among the slaves and secret learning
summary: Collins says slaves held clandestine services and his grandmother practiced piano on the quiet because reading and writing were illegal.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Do you remember any other stories from your grandmother about music?
Well, this was just the source for musical education.
Was there music amongst the slaves, or (inaudible). Were they allowed to go to church, did they have their own kind of --
Yes, they went to -- they had their own little church, they had their own services. They weren't allowed to participate because they weren't allowed to read or write. That was against the law.
Did they -- were they able to associate with eachother?
Yes, it was more of a clandestine thing.

But as you know it was against the law for them to read or write, so when she -- she had to practice the piano, you know, on the QT. You know, but she was a student to retain to absorb rather some of the -- most of the lessons.
